resolvedImplementation.semantics: Reads `process.argv` in the preload process and returns the value of a `--orca-browser-client-host-id=<id>` argument (or null if absent/empty). Source comments (browser-client-host-id-argument.ts:5-11) document WHY this is an argv read rather than a synchronous IPC call: Electron does not reliably answer a `sendSync` that arrives before its main-process listener registers (observed on Electron 43), leaving the renderer permanently blocked; an argv value is present from process birth. This method has no request/response and no subscription semantics whatsoever -- it is a pure local read.

resolvedImplementation.ipcShape: compound, but architecturally DIFFERENT from runtime-bridge.ts's own `subscribe` (PBR-007): ONE shared listener on the single static channel `runtimeEnvironments:subscriptionEvent` is created lazily (getOrCreateDispatcher, line 80-111) and multiplexes ALL concurrent subscriptions by a `subscriptionId` key in an in-memory Map, rather than one dedicated channel+listener per subscription.
resolvedImplementation.semantics: WeakMap keyed by IPC instance owns one dispatcher and callback map keyed by subscriptionId. Callbacks inserted BEFORE invoke; mismatched response ID or invoke rejection removes current map entry. Response/binary route to callbacks; error is non-terminal and retains entry. Close deletes entry and releases idle listener BEFORE calling onClose. unsubscribe always invokes runtimeEnvironments:unsubscribe for its ID even if already removed; only local dispatcher/listener removal waits for the last map entry. sendBinary sends subscriptionBinary. ID uses crypto.randomUUID, with Date.now/Math.random fallback. Source behavior only, not proof remote errors/cancellation handled end-to-end.

resolvedImplementation.semantics: Push callback to module array; attach one shared terminal:file-drop listener when not registered. Events iterate Array.from(callbacks). Disposer uses indexOf(callback) then splice one matching entry, removes shared listener only when empty. It is not a unique registration token: if identical function is registered repeatedly, a repeated disposer can remove another matching entry. Do not infer exactly-once/idempotent per-registration disposal.
